decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.
Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.
Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: [insert plan numbers/documents].
Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.
Condition : 3 - The materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall match those used in the existing building, unless otherwise shown on the approved plans.
Reason: In order to safeguard the appearance of the area.
Condition : 4 - No additional windows or openings shall be formed in the side elevations of the development hereby permitted.
Reason: In order to protect neighbours' privacy.
Condition : 5 - The roof area of the extension hereby permitted shall not be used as a balcony, roof garden or similar amenity area.
Reason: In order to protect neighbours' privacy
Condition : 6 - Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development Order) 1995 (or any order revoking or re-enacting that order), no enlargement of the premises or any additional structures/buildings/enclosures within the curtilage of the site shall be carried out, other than as shown in the approved drawings, and no additional floor space shall be formed within the building(s) hereby permitted by means of internal horizontal division (new mezzanine level) without prior written approval of the local planning authority.
Reason:  To protect neighbours' living conditions and the character and appearance of the area and to prevent over-intensive use of the site. 
Condition : 7 - All rainwater pipes, gutters, and associated fittings serving the existing and proposed dwellings hereby permitted shall be retained and thereafter maintained within the respective curtilage of each property. At no time shall any such features be positioned so as to discharge onto, overhang, or encroach upon adjoining land.
Reason:
To ensure that drainage arrangements are appropriately contained within the site, to safeguard neighbouring amenity, and to prevent any adverse impacts arising from surface water run-off, in accordance with good planning practice.
Condition : 8 - Prior to the commencement of development, (excluding demolition and site clearance), details of the final design of a surface water drainage scheme have been submitted to and approved in writing by the planning authority. The final solution should follow the principles set out in the approved drainage strategy. The design must satisfy the SuDS Hierarchy and be compliant with the National Standards for SuDS, NPPF and Ministerial Statement on SuDS. The required drainage details shall include:

a. The results of infiltration testing completed in accordance with BRE Digest 365 and confirmation of groundwater levels. Where infiltration is proposed confirmation is required of a 1m unsaturated zone from the base of any proposed soakaway to the seasonal high groundwater level and confirmation of half-drain times. 
b. Evidence that the receiving surface water sewer has onward connectivity and capacity to receive flows from the site.
c. Hydraulic calculations to demonstrate the proposed final solution will effectively manage the 1 in 30 (+30% allowance for climate change) 1 in 100 (+40% allowance for climate change) storm events and 10% allowance for urban creep. If infiltration is deemed unfeasible, associated discharge rates and storage volumes shall be provided using a maximum discharge rate of 0.5 l/s.
d. Detailed design drawings for all sustainable drainage elements including cross sections and detailed drainage layout plan.
e. An exceedance flow routing plan demonstrating no increase in surface water flood risk on or off site. The plan must include proposed levels and flow directions.
f. Details of drainage management responsibilities and maintenance regimes for all drainage elements.

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the agreed details and retained and maintained thereafter.

Reasons: To provide a sustainable development and to comply with policy EQ3 of the Hounslow Local Plan and guidance within the NPPF
Condition : 9 - No development shall take place until the applicant has entered into a binding arrangement with the Council to make an agreed contribution to the Council's Carbon Offset Fund, in accordance with the zero carbon strategy set out in the Energy Statement hereby approved to an amount that equates to the shortfall in required energy savings to meet the 'zero carbon' target.
Reason: In order to ensure the development meets sustainability standards. 
Condition : 10 - a)	The development hereby permitted shall be implemented in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy.
b)	Prior to first occupation of the new dwelling hereby approved, the relevant evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method) shall be submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing to show that the development has been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy, and any subsequent approved revisions.
c)	Prior to first occupation of the new dwelling hereby approved, where the post-construction evidence submitted pursuant to Part (b) demonstrates that an additional carbon offset contribution is required to achieve compliance with the zero-carbon requirements of the Development Plan, the applicant shall enter into a binding agreement with the Local Planning Authority to pay the additional amount. Such payment shall be calculated at the published carbon offset rate in force at the time the details required by Part (a) are submitted and shall be limited to any sum exceeding the contribution already secured and paid pursuant to Condition 8.
Reason: In order to ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.
Condition : 11 - (A) No development above ground level shall take place until details have been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority which demonstrate that:
(i)	At least three of the key elements of the building envelope (external walls, windows roof, upper floor slabs, internal walls, floor finishes/coverings) are to achieve a rating of A+ to D in the Building Research Establishment (BRE) The Green Guide of specification.
(ii)	At least 50% of timber and timber products are to be sourced from accredited Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) or Programme for the Endorsement of Forestry Certification (PEFC) scheme.
(iii)	No construction or insulation materials are to be used which would release toxins into the internal and external environment, including those that deplete stratospheric ozone.
(B) The development shall not be occupied until evidence (e.g. photographs and copies of installation contracts) has been submitted to the local planning authority to demonstrate that the development has been carried out in accordance with the approved details under Part A of this condition. The development shall be maintained in accordance with the approved details at all times thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of sustainable development.
Condition : 12 - Prior to first occupation of the building(s) hereby approved, the development shall have been constructed to achieve an internal water use of 105 litres/person/day or less.
Reason: In order to protect and conserve water supplies and resources.
Condition : 13 - Prior to the first occupation of the new dwelling hereby approved , the cycle parking facilities as shown on the approved site plan (ref: 582-A12B) shall be provided in full, and shall thereafter be retained for use at all times without obstruction. The cycle parking provision shall accord with the standards set out in the West London Cycle Parking Guidance. 
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.
Condition : 14 - The vehicular access to both dwellings hereby approved must be constructed in accordance with the submitted drawings. Each off-street parking area must be a minimum of 4.8 metres deep and a minimum of 2.4 metres wide. 

Reason: In order to protect the appearance of the and in the interests of highway safety.
Condition : 15 - Before the vehicle accesses hereby approved is first brought into use, the existing vehicular access on the approved site plan (ref: 582-A12B) shall be permanently closed and footway reinstated so that it cannot be used as an access across the pavement.
Reason: In order to enhance the pedestrian environment and to confine vehicular access to the permitted points to ensure that the development does not prejudice the free flow of traffic or highway safety along the adjacent highway.
Condition : 16 - Either side of the vehicle access hereby approved, visibility splay areas (the depth measured from the back of the footway and the widths outwards from the edges of the access, with a splay of at least 2.4 metres x 2.4 metres) shall be provided before the access and parking area is brought into use.  These areas shall be kept clear of any obstructions to visibility greater than 600 mm in height, including shrubs, planting, boundary walls, fences, gates, other means of enclosure or other structures or objects at all times.
Reason:  To ensure adequate visibility for drivers entering and leaving the site in the interests of pedestrian and vehicle safety.
Condition : 17 - Before the development is first brought into use, the boundary treatment as shown within approved drawings shall be erected and shall be retained permanently thereafter.

Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions and to ensure a satisfactory appearance.

Condition : 18 - Before the development hereby approved is first occupied, the developer shall make available to both dwellings a set of containers required at the time of development for household use for the storage and collection of recyclable materials for the purposes of the Council's kerbside recycling service, to the specification then in use by the local authority's recycling collection service and shall notify the Council's refuse and recycling services when the development is first occupied.  The waste and recyclable materials containers shall be stored in a proprietary refuse bin enclosure designed for the purpose to be supplied by the developer and located adjacent to each dwelling. Each dwelling with a private garden shall also be supplied with a garden waste composting bin of at least 220 litres capacity at the same time.
Reason: In order to protect the quality of the local environment and neighbours' living conditions and to endure appropriate means of refuse storage are provided.
description: Erection of a front porch extension. Formation of a vehicular access and extension and reconfiguration of an existing vehicular access. Erection of a two storey house with associated amenity space, car parking, cycle & refuse storage.
